opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: The labs: developing new vaccines and drugs. Down 27% — late-stage infectious-disease trials finished and wound down, plus deliberate cost cuts.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Sales teams, offices, admin. Up 5% — modest, the company is holding this line flat.

follow100Note: The striking thing: R&D eats $44 of every $100 — more than four times the operating profit it leaves behind. Moderna is still a research company that happens to sell vaccines, not a vaccine company with a research arm.
footerNote: Other income is $62M of interest less $21M of other expense, net $41M.
oneTimers: The 2026 full-year cost-of-sales outlook (~$1.7B) includes a ~$0.9B non-recurring litigation-settlement charge booked earlier in 2026 — it is not in Q3's $318M, but it is why the 9-month cost of sales ($1,366M) looks so much bigger than last year's ($416M). The $950M cash payment for that settlement went out in Q3.
On October 28, 2026, Moderna and GSK settled all pending disputes in the U.S. and Europe with patent cross-licenses — no payments of any kind under that deal.

In September, Moderna raised ~$2.6B net from a ~$3.0B convertible-notes offering (after capped-call costs). That financing — not operations — is the main reason cash jumped from $6.9B (June 30) to $8.0B (September 30). Nine-month operating cash flow is still negative at −$2,715M, and the 9-month net loss is −$1,963M: the Q3 profit does not make the year profitable.
otherDetail: Interest income of $62M, less $21M of other expense — net $41M.

segments.name: Net product sales
segments.note: Almost all of Moderna's money is selling vaccines — mainly COVID vaccines, now in the fall season, plus the newer flu and RSV shots.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Grants, collaborations, licensing and royalties — small side income, not product sales.

takeaways.text: Net income of $162M vs a $200M loss a year ago. The swing came from two directions at once: revenue up 29% and R&D down 27%. Either alone wouldn't have done it.
takeaways.title: Back in the black — but read the fine print

takeaways.text: Full-year revenue growth 15–25% (was up to 10%), R&D cut to ~$2.7B, year-end cash $8.1–8.3B (was $4.7–5.2B). Management is signaling the turnaround is real, not one good quarter.
takeaways.title: Guidance went up everywhere it matters

takeaways.text: Positive Phase 3 data for intismeran (Moderna's personalized cancer vaccine with Merck's Keytruda: 42% lower risk of melanoma recurrence or death) plus FDA approval of mFLUSIVA, a seasonal flu vaccine — Moderna's fifth approved product. The next chapter is oncology, not COVID.
takeaways.title: The pipeline is the story now

verdict: Moderna swung back to a profit on 29% revenue growth, but the profit is thin and the cost cuts did as much work as the sales rebound — and the fat cash balance came from a $3 billion convertible-note raise, not from operations.
